newHazards.summary: Staff basis now counts DRAFT payments on VOID invoices, and voidInvoiceInTx does NOT cascade payment status — LEAD RULING, not drift. voidInvoiceInTx (:4057-4061) only does `tx.invoice.updateMany({ where: { id, status: { not: VOID } }, data: { status: VOID } })`; no InvoicePayment write follows, so a DRAFT payment survives its invoice being voided and is now counted in the tile. The design of record allowed either shape ("EXCLUDING only VOID invoices (or whatever the memo excluded — quote it)"); the memo excluded nothing, so the executor excluded nothing, which is the faithful read. If the lead prefers the narrower `invoice: { status: { not: VOID } }`, it is one line here plus the m7 pin — but that would NOT reproduce the memo, and the E2E's `before + 2` delta oracle passes either way, so it must be a deliberate ruling made before landing rather than after.

The restored count has no `limit: 999` cap the memo had, so on a tenant with >999 invoices the tile can now read HIGHER than it did pre-#656. This is a correctness improvement (the cap was the F16/B12 bug), not a regression — but it means the post-deploy expectation is "the number may move up on large tenants", not "identical to pre-#656". Worth one line in the landing note so a jump is not misread as a new defect.

openApp() couples REG-B80/B144/B110 to the /invoices page's health: all three now load /invoices and wait on its "New Invoice" button before navigating to their own destination (/finance/payments/:id, /orders, /customers/:id), so an unrelated invoices-page regression would fail three tests for the wrong reason. review.reasoning:
Refute-first, and all three lead-named hazards were hunted and refuted rather than assumed.

K1(a) is the load-bearing claim and it holds under a side-by-side read I did myself, not from the executor's summary. The memo's payment loop (19a419ba page.tsx:270-272) sits ABOVE the first `if (inv.status !== …)` branch, so the memo's basis is genuinely "every invoice of every status", and the fix's staff branch carries no invoice-status filter at all. The buyer branch reproduces findAll's exact two rules (:2829-2832). The chain from that basis change to the observed failure is complete and mechanical: bare POST /invoices → DRAFT (schema default), recomputeStatus:283-289 makes DRAFT terminal so the $100 PAID payment cannot move it, KPI_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED contains DRAFT, so both fixture payments were dropped → the log's Expected "2" / Received "0".

The one thing that could have made this a one-more-round is tenant isolation: dropping the `invoice` relation filter for staff leaves the count with a bare `{ status: "DRAFT" }`. I verified the prisma tenant extension's switch puts "count" in the same branch as findMany/findFirst (`args.where = { ...args.where, tenantId }`), so scoping never depended on the relation filter. The query is also strictly cheaper than before (no join). No leak, no perf risk.

K1(b) needed no product change and got none — the summary key already shares the ["invoices"] prefix on production. I enumerated the mutation paths myself across the whole web api layer, including the five outside invoices.ts (credit-notes ×2, estimates, orders, payment-requests) and the realtime socket hook, and confirmed bookkeeping's /payments endpoint is a bookkeeping transaction, not an InvoicePayment. The new RTL guard is not vacuous: my own probe (removing only the ["invoices"] invalidation from useRecordInvoicePayment) turned it red at the right line, which is the half the executor's re-key probe did not cover; the file was restored and git confirms it unmodified.

The "e2e change beyond the token" concern is real in the literal sense — apiBase(BASE) became apiBase(page.url()) — but I checked playwright.config.ts and the two expressions are the same string, with apiBase stripping the path via new URL().origin. No assertion, oracle or fixture in those three tests changed; only the token acquisition and ten `headers` → `headers!` shorthands the nullable return forces. And tsc genuinely covers the e2e directory here (40 e2e files in --listFilesOnly), so those non-null assertions were typechecked rather than shipped unproven — the specs are never run locally, so that mattered.

The "m7 pin now vacuous" worry is the opposite of true: toBeUndefined() forbids any invoice-relation filter for staff, which is stricter than the exact-set assertion it replaced, and the test now also asserts the count is threaded to the response.

I re-ran the api invoices lane (318 passed), the full web lane (182 passed), prettier on all four files, and web lint (0 errors) rather than taking the gate report on trust. The four hazards I filed are all low and none blocks: the VOID-invoice question is a ruling the design explicitly delegated and the executor correctly surfaced rather than silently narrowed; the uncapped count and the openApp coupling are landing-note items; the nullable tenantId is pre-existing on production. Land.
